summary: @types-beta/sdk silently launches bundled Windows binary with remote-agent semantics on import
details: On import, dist/init.js unconditionally invokes init(), which on Windows spawns the bundled vendor/nanocache.exe as a detached, hidden-window child process with stdio ignored and child.unref(), so the opaque native binary survives the parent Node process. Any consumer that requires or imports @types-beta/sdk executes this ~1.15 MB Windows PE without prompt, consent, or configuration. Strings inside the PE (`/ws/agent`, `disconnect`, `update`, `exit_code`) are consistent with a WebSocket-based remote-control agent that connects outbound to accept commands and report exit codes, providing a persistent remote channel into the installer's host. The package is published as `@types-beta/sdk`, exploiting the `@types/*` type-definitions naming convention, and its README explicitly contrasts itself with `@types-beta/node` ("type definitions only and never executes code") — a cover story that misrepresents an import-time native-binary launcher as a routine typings-adjacent SDK.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
